inspection_summary: Fresh isolated inspection of all 1,189 logical lines in the exact SHA-bound normalized source. Eight conservative semantic units were retained from the toric-geometric core: encode an equivariant space by a base skeleton plus fiber-collapse data; use integral points to index sections and monomials; realize blow-up as local polytope surgery while exposing the boundary of toric representability; detect local quotient singularities by the index of the vanishing-cycle sublattice; recover non-toric objects as hypersurfaces in a richer toric ambient space; reverse face dimensions through reflexive duality; compress open dual data from rays to a lower-dimensional lattice; and use failed physical representations to distinguish local diagram validity from global contractibility and usefulness. The source's brane and mirror-symmetry passages are treated as physical dictionary or explicitly non-rigorous intuition, not proof of the mathematical toric claims. Novelty is unconfirmed because no #44 record, other corpus source, prior plan, alternate version, issue history, network resource, or corpus identity was consulted. Figures carry essential incidence information and OCR damage affects cycle labels, exponents, fractions, and formulas, so exact diagrammatic or algebraic reuse requires the typeset source.

accepted_units.title: Encode an equivariant space by a skeleton and its collapsing fibers
accepted_units.why_material: The source replaces a space with a lower-dimensional orbit coordinate together with a generic circle fiber and marks the boundary loci where that fiber collapses. The half-line and interval models separate three roles: the base records orbit position, collapse loci recover fixed points, and interval length records geometric size while translation of the interval origin changes nothing. The reusable move is to compress geometry without discarding degeneration data, and to state which coordinates in the compressed representation are gauge-like rather than intrinsic.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit is demonstrated for the complex plane and projective line; later examples generalize it to higher-dimensional torus fibers and faces. The source is a review for physicists rather than a formal proof treatment. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: the circle-action formula and metric coordinate are OCR-damaged, and the figures are unavailable; exact conventions require the PDF. Representation limit: the skeleton is meaningful only together with fiber and collapse labels, not as an unadorned interval. Scope limit: these examples rely on a torus action with controlled fixed loci; an arbitrary fibration or quotient need not be reconstructible from this skeletal data.

accepted_units.title: Turn an integral base into an index set for global sections
accepted_units.why_material: Adding a line bundle forces the interval length into an integral lattice, and lattice points then index the holomorphic sections. This connects a geometric quantization condition, a discrete polytope, and an algebraic basis without requiring evaluation of the sections. The semantic mechanism is that an integral structure upgrades a continuous orbit-space representation into a finite combinatorial catalogue of allowed global objects.
accepted_units.context_note: The source establishes the dictionary in the projective-line example and later extends it to projective-space polytopes and hypersurface monomials. The physical Bohr-Sommerfeld analogy is supporting intuition, not an additional proof. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: the Chern-class and section formulas contain OCR errors, though the prose correspondence is clear. Representation limit: the encoding depends on a chosen line bundle and integral moment-polytope normalization. Scope limit: lattice points count the relevant sections in this toric setting; arbitrary bundles, nonintegral classes, or non-toric spaces do not inherit this indexing rule without further hypotheses.

accepted_units.title: Represent blow-up by local polytope surgery and mark where the representation stops
accepted_units.why_material: Blowing up a torus-fixed point is translated into replacing a vertex by an interval, with the interval length measuring the exceptional divisor. The same passage then supplies the crucial failure mode: symmetry can move only finitely many generic points to toric vertices, and further corner blow-ups represent special configurations rather than generic ones; the resulting geometry can change with point position. This is a reusable discipline for combinatorial models: pair the local surgery rule with an explicit characterization of the moduli it cannot encode.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction is illustrated for projective-plane blow-ups and the source distinguishes generic del Pezzo blow-ups from special toric ones. Exact incidence is figure-dependent. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: the surgery is primarily shown in a missing figure, and some group/Chern-class labels are corrupted. Representation limit: the polytope cut encodes blow-up at a torus-fixed vertex, not arbitrary point-position data. Scope limit: local similarity of the surgery does not imply that repeated special-position blow-ups share the positivity or deformation class of generic blow-ups.

accepted_units.title: Detect a quotient singularity from failure of vanishing cycles to generate the lattice
accepted_units.why_material: At a vertex, the cycles collapsing along incident faces span a full-rank sublattice of the torus-cycle lattice. Equality of the two lattices gives the smooth local model; finite index leaves a finite quotient group and produces a local quotient singularity. Because smoothness propagates along faces adjacent to a smooth vertex, the global toric smoothness check reduces to the zero-dimensional strata. The generic move is to convert local geometric regularity into an exact generation test and then minimize verification to canonical strata.
accepted_units.context_note: The source states this as the general smoothness consideration for toric varieties and illustrates it with cyclic quotient singularities. It does not provide a full formal toric proof. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: cycle labels and the example's indices are OCR-damaged; the lattice quotient statement is prose-readable but exact labels require the PDF. Representation limit: the test presupposes the toric face/cycle dictionary and primitive lattice data. Scope limit: checking vertices suffices in the stated toric setting; non-toric singularities, non-simplicial behavior, stack structures, or incorrectly normalized cycle generators require additional analysis.

accepted_units.title: Recover a non-toric object by imposing equations in a richer toric ambient space
accepted_units.why_material: When the target object itself lacks torus symmetry, the source embeds it as the zero locus of a line-bundle section in a higher-dimensional toric space. Integral polytope points index the monomial deformations of the defining equation, while a controlled coefficient limit degenerates the object to the union of toric boundary faces. The reusable move is to trade direct representability for an ambient representation that preserves combinatorial access to deformations and a tractable limiting model.
accepted_units.context_note: The passage treats Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces, beginning with degree-defined hypersurfaces in projective space. The generic hypersurface is explicitly noted not to retain the ambient torus symmetry. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: degree, monomial, coefficient-limit, and fiber-dimension formulas are damaged and need typeset verification. Representation limit: the object is represented by ambient toric data plus an equation; the polytope alone no longer determines the generic hypersurface. Scope limit: smoothness, Calabi-Yau status, and faithfulness of the degeneration require the appropriate line bundle and genericity assumptions; arbitrary equations or ambient spaces need not behave similarly.

accepted_units.title: Use reflexivity to make polar duality integral and reverse face dimensions
accepted_units.why_material: Polar duality converts each supporting face into a dual vertex and, more generally, a face of one dimension into a complementary-dimensional face. Integrality is not automatic; requiring both the polytope and its polar to be integral singles out reflexive polytopes. In the source, that same condition matches the anticanonical bundle requirement for the hypersurface, and the origin supplies the distinguished boundary-product deformation. The reusable pattern is to identify the compatibility condition that makes a dual representation stay inside the original discrete category.
accepted_units.context_note: The source states the face correspondence, involutive reflexivity, and equivalence with the Calabi-Yau hypersurface condition, citing Batyrev. Its later physical mirror explanation is explicitly non-rigorous and is not used to strengthen these claims. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: the polar inequality, dimension indices, and line-bundle equation are OCR-damaged; exact conventions require the PDF. Representation limit: the construction depends on an integral polytope with the origin in its interior and a chosen lattice pairing. Scope limit: a polar of an arbitrary integral polytope need not be integral, and reflexive duality of ambient polytopes does not by itself prove every asserted mirror-symmetry property.

accepted_units.title: Compress open dual rays when one coordinate is globally fixed
accepted_units.why_material: For an open toric variety, the source replaces bounded polar faces by rays normal to the original faces. In the Calabi-Yau local models considered, every ray has the same final coordinate, reflecting a fixed normal-circle contribution. Removing that redundant coordinate leaves a finite point configuration in a lattice of one lower dimension without losing the face-normal data. The generic move is to prove a coordinate is constant for structural reasons before quotienting it away as redundant.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction is illustrated on local surface and canonical-bundle examples and is presented as an extension of compact polytope duality. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: several ray coordinates and example point lists are corrupted; exact configurations require typeset figures/formulas. Representation limit: dimension reduction depends on all rays lying in a common affine hyperplane fixed by the Calabi-Yau normal direction. Scope limit: general open toric varieties may not have this common-coordinate property, so projecting rays can otherwise lose scale or incidence information.

accepted_units.title: Use diagram pathologies to audit representability, contractibility, and usefulness separately
accepted_units.why_material: The source translates parallel or intersecting external lines in a brane diagram back into zero or negative first-Chern behavior on a corresponding curve, then applies a negativity criterion to explain why a locally sensible configuration cannot shrink at finite moduli distance. It distinguishes three questions that a representation can easily conflate: whether the local object exists, whether it admits the required global contraction, and whether the alternative representation is actually useful for extracting results. The failure points toward a richer construction in a higher-dimensional ambient space with equations.
accepted_units.context_note: The Chern-class and contraction discussion uses established geometry, while the surrounding brane interpretation and proposed future configurations are physical and partly speculative. The unit retains the methodological separation, not the speculative brane proposals. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: the relevant diagram is unavailable and some bundle/Chern labels are damaged; exact incidence and signs require the PDF. Representation limit: the diagnostic translation relies on the toric/brane dictionary and a curve represented by the bounded interval. Scope limit: Grauert-type negativity has precise analytic hypotheses, and the source's physical conclusion about critical theories does not follow for arbitrary diagrams; an alternative representation's existence also does not guarantee its usefulness.

ecosystem_findings.summary: Within this source, representation change ranges from loss-aware skeletonization to local polytope surgery, ambient lifting by equations, structurally justified dimension reduction, and explicit failure audits. This strengthens a source-only probe that asks what data each representation preserves, what it forgets, and when a richer ambient encoding is necessary. Corpus novelty is unconfirmed.

The source uses integral lattices, indices, monomials, and reflexive polytopes, but its mathematical mechanisms are toric combinatorics and complex geometry rather than arithmetic geometry in the usual number-theoretic sense. It therefore challenges routing based only on words such as integral or lattice. Whether this corrects any actual #44 assignment is unconfirmed because #44 was not inspected.

The source makes local geometry depend not only on which fiber cycles vanish, but on whether their primitive classes generate the full integral lattice: finite index becomes a finite quotient singularity. This is a source-grounded candidate geometry dependency; novelty elsewhere in the ecosystem is unconfirmed.

Point positions, line-bundle coefficients, and contraction limits show that a combinatorial presentation can cover only a special locus in a larger moduli problem. This strengthens a source-only probe for distinguishing parameters encoded by a representation from moduli it silently freezes or omits. Corpus novelty is unconfirmed.
